answer: To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and open the Stores section. Use the Most Abandoned Products report to see which products visitors placed in a cart but didn't buy, and the Abandoned Carts Funnel, Abandoned Carts Funnel Over Time, or Abandoned Carts Summary reports to study abandoned and recovered carts in detail (including filters for product gross value and customer type). The Store Conversion Funnel report also shows the 'added to cart' step in the customer journey. To see how items were sold, use the Sales by Product Variant report (shows which variants like size and color are selling most) and the Sales by item report in the Sales reports section (breakdown of specific items and services sold, viewable by orders, items, and customers).

To rename a web link in your site menu: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Select Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

To update the share image (og:image), go to Pages & Menu in the Editor, click the relevant page, click More Actions, select Social share, click Upload Image, select your image, click Add to Page, and then Publish your site. You can also set one og:image for the entire site. Ensure your image meets the recommended size of 1200 x 630 pixels (aspect ratio 1.91:1, max 8MB; minimum 200 x 200 px but 600 x 315 px recommended to avoid small previews). If you recently updated the og:image and it still shows the old image, enter your site URL in the Facebook debugger to refresh the cached information. Note that on LinkedIn, after changing page information it can take up to a week for the new image to appear in shares, and you can use the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) to check the preview. For Wix Forum posts specifically, the displayed image is the first image in the forum post, or if none, the image from your site's social tab (set via Settings > Website Settings > General social image).

To add a personalized name to your automated emails using dynamic values: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard and edit the automation with the 'Send an email' action. Click the 'Send an email' action in your flow, then under 'Create an email' click Edit. Click the text element where you want to add the name, then click '+ Add Dynamic Value' (or '+ Add Personalized Content') and select the value from the drop-down menu (e.g., contact first name). Optionally enter fallback text to display if the data is unavailable. Click Save. Note: Personalized content does not appear in test emails, but recipients will see it when the automation is sent.

No, Wix Stores is designed for selling physical and digital products, not services. To sell services such as workshops, courses, or private sessions, you should use Wix Bookings, which lets members book and pay for services online.

In the Wix Editor, a mobile-friendly version of your site is automatically created using the content from your desktop site. To adjust how your site looks on mobile, open the mobile Editor and either drag elements to different locations or use the Page Layout Optimizer tool (click Page Layout Optimizer on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click Optimize Now) to optimize the layout for smaller screens. Note: If you're using the latest Editor experience, the Page Layout Optimizer is not available because Wix automatically optimizes your mobile layout.

This behavior typically occurs when the image scaling setting on your strip is set to 'Tile' (which displays the image in tile formation across the space, making it appear to multiply) or 'Original Size' (which displays the original size and may cut off parts of the image). To fix this, go to your editor, select the image on the strip, click 'Change Strip Background' (or 'Change Column Background' if it's in a column), click 'Settings', scroll to 'Scaling & Positioning', and change 'How's the image scaled?' to 'Scale to Fill' so the image resizes to fill the available space. You can then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve it: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address again. If the error occurs on a dynamic page in your CMS, it may be because visitors lack permissions to access the collection; go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click the relevant collection, click More Actions, select Permissions & privacy, and edit the permissions to allow access. If the problem persists, contact Wix support.

To remove unwanted gaps at the bottom of your desktop page in the Wix Editor, you can try the following solutions from the spacing and alignment guide:

**If the gap is between your page content and the footer:**
- Adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon to remove the space between the content and footer. Note: If your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main page area.
- Alternatively, change the page design by selecting a different preset design, as some page designs can cause gaps between the body and footer.

**If the gap appears below the footer on your live site:**
- Change the page background color to match your footer color so the gap appears to be part of the footer.
- Add more content to your page to make it longer and cover the viewport.
- Resize your footer to make it longer, which can give your page extra length.
- Check the Layers panel for hidden elements that may be causing the gap, and delete or reposition them.

Note: Changes made in the mobile editor do not affect your desktop site, so ensure you are making these adjustments in the desktop editor.

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method), your site is already connected to Google. If your dynamic list page isn't sorting alphabetically on the published site despite having sort conditions set, check these common causes: 1) Verify your dataset mode is set to 'Read' or 'Read & Write' — datasets in 'Write' mode cannot read collection content or apply sorts. 2) Ensure your site has been published since you added the dynamic page or made the sort changes. 3) If you have the sandbox collection enabled, sync your sandbox collection to the live collection so the editor content matches the live site. 4) Note that dataset sorts override any 'Mirror on Site' collection order, so the dataset sort should take precedence — if it's not applying, the dataset mode or publish status is the likely issue.

It takes time for search engines to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, even after you've updated your site. Since you've already submitted your updated sitemap, the remaining options depend on your verification status: If you have verified your site with Google, you can submit a manual removal request through Google Search Console to speed up the removal of the old pages from search results. If you have not verified your site with Google or Bing, you will need to wait for the search engines to remove the pages on their own, as the removal process and timeline depends entirely on the individual search engines.

Documents may be rejected for several specific reasons. For your photo ID: it must be active/non-expired, in color, show all 4 borders and corners, not be blocked/blacked out, straightened (not angled), not blurry/overexposed/a screenshot, and your first/middle/last name and birth date in your Wix Payments account must match the ID exactly. For passports, the MRZ must be visible; for driver's licenses or government ID cards, send a separate file for each side. For address verification: the document must be visible/clear, dated within the last 6 months, and complete (at minimum one full page with full name and address visible). For bank documents (statement, voided check, or bank letter): they may be rejected if blurry, illegible, torn/damaged, rotated/upside down, a mobile screenshot, missing full account numbers, if the name/company doesn't match your account details, if account numbers are incorrect, if it's a direct deposit form instead of a bank statement, or if the voided check wasn't printed by a financial institution. For company documents: the tax ID/registration number and company name must be visible/clear and match your Wix Payments account, and the document must be issued within the last 12 months. All documents must be issued within the same country you selected as your business location (for business accounts, your ID may be from any Wix Payments supported country). Files must be in HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG format, max 10 MB, min 1 KB for PDF or 100 KB for other formats. If 7 business days have passed and you've verified your information is correct, contact Wix Customer Care.

The error likely occurs because the currency set in your Wix account does not match the currency in your payment provider account, or your payment provider does not support your site's currency. To resolve this: 1) Ensure your Wix site currency matches your payment provider account currency. To change your Wix currency, go to Settings in your site's dashboard, click Language & Region, scroll to Currency, select your currency from the drop-down, and click Save. 2) If your payment provider does not support your desired currency, you can change your payment provider to one that does, or contact your payment provider to change the currency in their account. 3) If payments are being declined specifically because the currency is not supported, contact your payment provider to confirm support, and either change your payment provider or change your currency for accepting payments.

To add a subscribe form to your site, the steps depend on whether you're using Wix ADI or the Wix Editor:

**If using Wix ADI:**
- To add to a page: Click **Add** on the top bar, click **Section to Page**, click **Subscribe**, then select the layout you want to use.
- To add to the footer (appears on all pages): Click the footer in the ADI builder, then select the checkbox next to **Subscribe** on the left.

**If using the Wix Editor (New Forms):**
- Go to your editor, click **Add Elements** on the left side, click **Contact & Forms**, scroll down to the **Subscribe** section, and drag a form onto your site.
- Click **Settings** to customize layout, design, and manage submissions.

**Alternative:** You can also add a 'subscribe to mailing list' checkbox field to any existing standalone form by clicking the form, selecting **Edit Form**, clicking **Subscribe**, and customizing the checkbox settings.

Everyone who signs up is automatically added to your contact list with a 'Subscriber' label.

To update the terms & conditions (policy) checkbox at checkout in Wix Stores: Go to Checkout Settings in your site's dashboard, click Customize your checkout, then click Policies. Select the checkbox next to the policy you want to display and enter the policy text. To make the checkbox appear at checkout, enable the Policy agreement checkbox toggle. You can also choose whether it is Checked by default (Selected = already checked; Deselected = customers must check it themselves to agree before completing checkout). Click Save. Note: Custom policies created via '+ Create Your Own Custom Policy' appear as links in the checkout footer but do not appear next to the policy checkbox.

Make sure you clicked Publish in your editor after entering the new Title tag, since changes only appear on the live site after publishing. If it still shows the old title, check whether any custom code added to your site is overriding the browser tab title and try removing that custom code. Also verify you are using a supported browser, and try viewing the live site in an incognito/private window or after clearing your browser cache and cookies to rule out a local caching issue.

Since you have a Google Workspace Admin account, you can reset the second business Gmail (user) password for them. Sign in to your Google Admin account, click Password, then Reset Password. Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a new one (by default the minimum length is 8 characters). Optionally click Preview to view it, enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle if you want the user to change it, then click Reset. You can then click 'Click to copy password' to paste it somewhere, or choose to email the password to the user, then click Done. If the user still can't verify their identity, you can also temporarily turn off the login challenge: in the Google Admin account click Login Challenge, then 'Turn off for 10 mins', then Done.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site: 1) In your Google Analytics account, copy your GA4 measurement ID from the Web stream details. 2) Go to Marketing Integrations on your Wix site's dashboard. 3) Click View under Google Analytics. 4) Click the Show More icon in the top right corner, then click Edit. 5) Paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up (ensure no extra spaces before the code). 6) Optionally select the IP Anonymization checkbox to hide visitor IP addresses. 7) Click Save.

When using Wix Payments, your payments are transferred as payouts directly to your bank account. Each payment goes through 3 stages before reaching your bank: (1) Processing (2-5 business days including settlement and pending periods), (2) Scheduled payout (added to your next daily, weekly, or monthly payout), and (3) Sent payout (funds sent from Wix Payments and arriving in your bank account within 3-5 business days). To receive payouts, your Wix Payments account must be verified and Active, with an available balance of at least $1. You can view your payout details and upcoming payouts in the Payouts section of your site's dashboard.

For a page without a footer, click on the page itself, then click and drag the Adjust Page Height handle located at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: this option is only available if you have selected the 'No Header & Footer' layout for that page. If the handle isn't moving, an element at the bottom of the page may be blocking the resize—you cannot make the page shorter if it would cut off an element. Move or delete the blocking element first; if you can't find it, use the Layers panel to locate it. You can also double-click the Adjust Page Height handle to reset the page height.

It is not possible to edit or modify a domain name once it has been purchased. To change your domain name (for example, to remove 'DBT'), you must register a new domain. Additionally, since domains purchased through Wix renew automatically, you should turn off the auto-renewal option for the old domain to avoid being charged for another year.

To sync an external calendar's iCal link with Wix Hotels so availability shows on your site: 1) Locate your iCal URL. 2) Go to your dashboard and click the Hotels tab. 3) Expand the Reservations tab and select iCal. 4) Click the Choose Type drop-down menu and select a room type. 5) Paste your iCal URL into the URL field. 6) (Optional) Click Add Calendar to add another room type and paste its iCal URL. 7) Click Save. Important: The sync is one-way only (from iCal to the Wix Calendar); imported rates do not appear in the calendar. If you have multiple room types, you must add a different iCal URL for each room type. This feature is not compatible with the Wix Hotels Channel Manager—if you want to connect the Channel Manager, delete all URLs in this tab first.

To transfer an edited page from your copy (duplicate) site back to your original site, use the copy and paste page feature between the two sites: 1) In the Editor of your copy site, click 'Menus & Pages' on the left side. 2) Right-click the page you edited and click 'Copy'. 3) Open the Editor of your original site. 4) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select 'Paste' (or 'Paste & Apply Site Theme' if you want to apply the original site's colors and fonts). 5) Rename the pasted page if needed and click 'Done'. Note: The pasted page is added as a main page to the Site Menu. You cannot copy anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, or pages from third-party/Wix business solution apps. If you have trouble pasting, your browser local storage may be full—clear it and try again.

To update the og:image for your entire site: Open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select an image or click + Upload Media to upload a new one, click Choose File, click Save at the top of the dashboard, and publish your site. The documentation states that the og:image is displayed when sharing your site on social networks such as Facebook, X, and LinkedIn, but it does not specifically mention whether this affects the image when links are posted in email or on Instagram.

To transfer an edited page from a copy site to your original site without overwriting the original page, copy the page from the copy site and paste it as a new page on the original site. Steps: 1) In the copy site's Editor, click Menus & Pages on the left side, right-click the page you want to transfer, and click Copy. 2) Open the Editor of your original site. 3) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme if you want to apply the original site's colors and fonts). 4) The pasted page is added as a new main page to the Site Menu—it does not overwrite your existing page. 5) Rename the new page (enter the new name and click Done) so you can distinguish it from the original page. You can then hide, delete, or keep the original page as needed.

To download your website visit reports, go to All Reports in your site's dashboard (under Analytics), select the relevant traffic report (such as Traffic over time), click the Download drop-down at the top right, and select a file format (Excel, CSV, or Image/PNG). You can download reports including their customized view, which allows you to export the data for your specified period (December 15 to January 15) in CSV or Excel format.

To cancel within the 14-day money-back period and receive a full refund, go to **Premium Subscriptions** in your Wix account, click the **More Actions icon** next to the relevant plan, then click **Cancel Plan** and **Cancel Now** to confirm. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan is immediately deactivated and your payment method is refunded automatically (allow up to 20 business days for the refund to appear on your statement). After canceling, your site reverts to the free Wix URL and displays Wix ads, but your content is not deleted.

To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) on a 64-bit JVM, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This removes the lower 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, allowing native memory to grow beyond 4GB. Note that this will result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so you should adjust the Java heap size to a larger value and monitor/retune garbage collection as required. You can verify the setting by checking the JVM arguments in the admin console, the ps output, or the javacore for the argument -Xnocompressedrefs.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985013. The bulletin states that IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker, upon installation on Unix platforms, set incorrect permissions for an object, exposing it to an unintended actor (CVE-2016-0394). The vulnerability could allow a local attacker to manipulate certain files. CVSS Base Score is 4.0 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N). For current V8 or V9 fix pack installations on Unix platforms, the bulletin provides mitigation commands to correct permissions on the <IIB install dir>/isadc directory: 'find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;', 'find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \;', and 'find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -name *.sh -print -exec chmod 755'.
The Sybase Server Agent 620 FP2 installer (6.2.0-TIV-ITM_SYB-FP0002) can be downloaded from IBM Passport Advantage using part number CNN25ML.

The errors indicate the WebSphere Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required to initialize SSL (HTTPS), causing the HTTPS transport to be skipped. To resolve this on Linux, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory bundled with the Plug-in. For a 64-bit Plug-in v8.x, use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/ . Note that for Apache on Linux, setting this from the command line prior to starting the web server may not work; instead, add the export command to /etc/sysconfig/httpd for RHEL Linux or /usr/sbin/envvars for SLES/SUSE Linux so the variable is set when the web server starts.

To resolve this error without installing a fix, apply the local fix documented in IBM PI34677: 1) Open the WAS admin console, 2) Navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties, 3) Locate the entry named 'ServerExt.applications' and review its value.

You can find the required authorizations by looking at the /IBMMON/AUTH profile available in the SAP Agent transport. This profile contains the minimum required authorization settings. Create your own userid and provide it with the same set of authorizations defined for the /IBMMON/AUTH profile to ensure the SAP agent performs successful data collection with a non-default userid.

Tune the sib.trm.linger property in the sib.properties file to control the messaging engine lookup delay (the WLM linger/wait time that causes the ~3000 ms sleep seen in the WaitForWLMDat trace). Set this property in either <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles in the installation) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile and takes precedence if defined in both locations). After modifying the property, restart the server.

In a clustered environment, the most likely causes for the latest ruleset not executing after a 'Replace RuleApp Version' deployment are: (1) the hot deploy notification was not sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) in the cluster, often due to insufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) for the user publishing the update, preventing JMX notification to all XUs; (2) asynchronous ruleset parsing is enabled, meaning while the updated ruleset is being parsed, an earlier version may still be used for executions; (3) the updated ruleset failed to parse successfully, causing the XU to fall back on an earlier active version that parses; or (4) the ruleset path requested by the client does not specify a version, though this would normally request the highest version. Verify that the publishing user has Monitor role permissions to ensure all cluster nodes receive the hot deploy notification, and check whether asynchronous parsing is delaying the switch to the new version.

The clearing event is not received because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after it receives the event, causing the event to be dropped before it appears in the EIF logs or OMNIbus. To resolve this, change the ConnectionMode in the om_tec.config file on the ITM Server (TEMS) from 'ConnectionMode=co' (connection oriented) to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on the ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

The error is caused by the Windows security policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' being enabled. To resolve, open Local Security Policy under Administrative Tools, navigate to Local Policies > Security Options, select 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' and set it to Disabled, then retry the key import. If this is a new server where encryption has not been set up, you may also need to export/generate the encryption keys first before importing.

Yes, IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance supports SHA-2 (SHA-256). When a Certificate Authority (CA) signs a certificate using SHA2 (SHA-256), DataPower can validate the CA's signature on the certificate while building the trust chain from the DataPower ValCred. This is supported in firmware versions 3.7.2, 3.7.3, 3.8, and 3.8.1.

The error IQQG0205E indicates that the version of the IBM Content Search Services client embedded in the IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine is not compatible with the IBM Content Search Services server version. The client and server versions must match. Check the readme files for your installed IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine and IBM Content Search Services fix packs to verify fix pack requirements and ensure compatible versions are installed (for example, IBM Content Search Services 5.2.1.5 fix pack requires specific Content Platform Engine fix packs such as 5.2.1.5-P8CPE-FP005).

In the db2diag.log corruption entry, locate the Obj={pool:X;obj:Y;type:Z} field. Here, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To find the object name, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>" (substituting the obj and pool values respectively).

When using compressed references on a 64-bit JVM, the Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks are stored using 32-bit fields and must therefore be allocated in the first 4GB of the address space (the low-memory region). Even if the Java heap is located above 4GB and the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust the low-memory region under 4GB. When the JVM later tries to allocate memory for an artifact that must reside in low-memory (because only a 32-bit pointer is reserved for it), it fails and throws a Native OutOfMemoryError (NOOM). To resolve this, you can use -Xgc:preferredHeapBase to place the heap above 4GB, or use -Xmcrs (available in Java 6.0.16.3, 6.1.8.3, 7.0.8.10, 7.1.2.10 and later) to reserve additional low-memory space at startup. If NOOM persists after these settings, investigate reducing the size and usage of Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks at the application level.

WebSphere Application Server is loading the JDBC driver class from whichever jar the classloader resolves first. When multiple versions of JDBC drivers from the same vendor (e.g., both ojdbc6.jar and ojdbc14.jar) are configured in different scopes (cell, node, server), there is a possibility of a collision of the classes and you cannot predict from which version of the driver jar the class got loaded. Even if the JDBC provider is pointed to ojdbc6.jar, if ojdbc14.jar is also present in another scope, the older driver class may be loaded instead, causing the SystemOut.log to show the older driver version (DSRA8206I). To resolve this, isolate the resource provider so that only the intended JDBC driver jar is available in the classpath for that data source.

To resize the image in your new section: click the image, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want (corner handles keep the original proportions). To add text on top of the image: click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click Box, drag a container box onto the image, make it transparent by clicking Change Design > Customize Design > Fill Color & Opacity and dragging the Background slider to 0%, then drag your text element onto the container box. Alternatively, to add text that appears when hovering over the image, click the image, click the Settings icon, and enter the text in the 'Does this image have a tooltip?' field.

The behavior you are experiencing is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the session timeout. In IBM Operational Decision Manager (ODM) Rule Team Server/Decision Center, the transaction timeout is set to 10 minutes (600 seconds) by default via the property `ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout` in the teamserver web module's WEB-INF/web.xml file. If a transactional operation (such as authoring rules in a large repository) takes longer than this timeout to complete, the transaction is rolled back and the user is effectively kicked out of the operation. To resolve this, you can increase the value of `ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout` (in seconds) in the web.xml file located in the RTS/DC EAR file (jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). Additionally, you should check application server specific transaction timeout configurations (e.g., for WebSphere Application Server, check the 'Maximum transaction timeout').

The error indicates the Centera SDK library (FPLibrary) is not found in java.library.path because changes to the setCenteraLibPath.sh or setCenteraLibPath file were not picked up by the WebSphere Application Server startup script. This typically occurs when the WAS Content Engine instance is restarted from within the WAS console rather than from the command line, causing the CenteraSDK path to not be loaded. To resolve: after making any changes to the setCenteraLibPath.sh or setCenteraLibPath.bat file, restart WebSphere from the IBM console (command line) so the changes are detected and the library path is properly loaded.

The information is available in the IBM Security Bulletin titled 'IBM MQ is affected by a potential denial of service to channel processes (CVE-2017-1557)'. According to this bulletin, an IBM MQ application with authority to connect to a remote queue manager could send a malicious request causing undefined behavior within the channel process servicing that connection, including loss of service for other connections on the same channel process. The vulnerability (CVE-2017-1557) allows an authenticated user with authority to send a specially crafted request that could cause a channel process to cease processing further requests. CVSS Base Score is 4.3.

The information is available in the IBM Security Bulletin document swg22003510.txt. This bulletin covers CVE-2017-1236, where IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user to potentially cause a denial of service by issuing an incorrect saved channel status inquiry. The CVSS Base Score is 3.1 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). Affected products include IBM MQ 9.0.2 Continuous Delivery, IBM MQ Appliance 9.0.x Continuous Delivery, and IBM MQ 9.0 LTS. The current temporal score can be found at https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/124354.

To identify indexing errors in the Atlas database:

1. Login to the Atlas database as the PSSAPL user.
2. Run the query: `select * from ctx_user_index_errors;`
3. Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY field from the results.
4. Run the query: `select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>';`
5. This will list the document that has the indexing error.

Note: Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors.

This is a known DB2 11 for z/OS defect documented in APAR PI19804. SQLCODE -401 (DSNT408I) with SQLERRP=DSNXOBFC occurs when creating a native SQL procedure that contains a control statement (such as an IF statement) with an IN-LIST predicate referencing SQL variables. DB2 11 does not process the SQL variables in the IN-LIST predicate properly, resulting in the incorrect SQLCODE -401 (or potentially ABEND0C4/ABEND04E). The issue affects all DB2 11 for z/OS users of compiled SQL scalar functions or native SQL procedures with this pattern. A fix is available for APAR PI19804 (closed as program error); obtain and apply the PTF for this APAR to resolve the issue.

According to the supported operating system matrix, Apple Macintosh OS X 10.9 (Mavericks) only supports IBM SPSS Statistics 22 and IBM SPSS Statistics 23. The IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription installer (which corresponds to newer releases such as Statistics 24 or 25) is not supported on OS X 10.9.5. To install a newer Subscription version, you must upgrade your Mac OS to at least macOS 10.12 (Sierra) for Statistics 24 or macOS 10.13 (High Sierra) for Statistics 25. Alternatively, if you must remain on OS X 10.9.5, you can only install SPSS Statistics 22 (with Apple Java SE 6 installed first) or Statistics 23.

The error is caused by a corrupt installation of the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API. To resolve this, re-install the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API: 1) Copy the software to a local disk, 2) Start the re-installation of the .NET API, 3) Select all sub-components of .NET Framework 4.5 that were not listed before (select them all if unsure). During the next installation of ICC there will be no further errors regarding missing components.

Theme files and other portal resources are served from the browser or proxy cache (HTTP 304) rather than from the server because a long cache was set and the resolver uses a digest to cache URLs like resource aggregator collections. This digest remains the same between server restarts, so updated theme resources are not re-fetched. To force the browser to load the updated resources, set the "digest.seed" key in the WP ConfigService to any string value; this generates a new digest on server boot and forces a digest change during restart. Alternatively, users can manually clear the browser cache or press Ctrl+F5 to bypass the cache.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, use the mqsichangeproperties command to generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group: mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core. The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Note that collection of Java core dumps is an invasive activity and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.
